question: A bought an item for ₹384 and sold it for ₹480. B bought another item for ₹1,254 and sold it for ₹1,672. What is the ratio of the gain percentage of A to the gain percentage of B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Gain % of **A** = (480 − 384) ÷ 384 × 100 = 96 ÷ 384 × 100 = 25%.

Gain % of **B** = (1672 − 1254) ÷ 1254 × 100 = 418 ÷ 1254 × 100 = 33.33% or (100/3)%.

**Ratio** = 25 ÷ (100/3) = 25 × 3 ÷ 100 = 75 ÷ 100 = 3/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CPA = ₹384, SPA = ₹480 | CPB = ₹1,254, SPB = ₹1,672.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/85e1f847aac0d5ca6019fa91bd480cc6c17deabafff0d6536433ef2abf3f9e1e.png] 

⇒ **Gain for A** = 480 − 384 = 96.

⇒ **Gain % of A (GA)** = (96 ÷ 384) × 100 = 25%.

⇒ **Gain for B** = 1672 − 1254 = 418.

⇒ **Gain % of B (GB)** = (418 ÷ 1254) × 100 = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 100/3%.

⇒ **Ratio (GA : GB)** = 25 : (100/3) = 75 : 100 = 3 : 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Gain and Loss Concepts

Profit occurs when **Selling Price (SP)** is greater than **Cost Price (CP)**. Gain% is always calculated on the **CP** unless stated otherwise.

Ratio of Percentages

When finding the **ratio of two percentages**, the 100 in the denominator cancels out, essentially comparing the decimal or fractional multipliers directly.
